title: VPS or shared hosting: which one pays off for your site on Hostinger
seoTitle: VPS or shared hosting: which to choose
description: An ordinary site does fine on shared hosting; a VPS only with your own system, reserved resources or root access. Chart by scenario and KVM specs.
metaDescription: VPS or shared hosting at Hostinger: what each one is, a chart by scenario, the specs of KVM 1 to 8 and what maintenance is left to you.

contentSections.heading: Quick answer
paragraphs: For a blog, portfolio or small shop, start by comparing shared plans that support your application. Consider a VPS when you need software, configuration or root access those plans do not provide, and someone to maintain the server. The code SONAR20 gives 20% off new purchases of either, not renewals or domains.

contentSections.heading: What each one is
paragraphs: **Shared hosting** is one server split between several customers. Hostinger looks after the operating system, the web server and the updates; you log in to the control panel, install WordPress or upload your site's files, and that is it. At Hostinger, these are the Single, Premium and Unlimited plans, plus Cloud Startup, which is the same idea with more resources.

A **VPS** (virtual private server) is a virtual machine of your own, with reserved processor, memory and disk, plus root access, the system administrator account. You take responsibility for configuration, updates and security. The plans compared here are KVM 1, 2, 4 and 8.
The difference is not “better or worse”. It is who looks after the server and how much of its resources are reserved for you.

contentSections.heading: Which to choose, by scenario
paragraphs: Before you look at prices, answer three questions. If the answer is “no” to all three, shared hosting will do.

contentSections.heading: The VPS plans: KVM 1 to 8
paragraphs: The four KVM plans differ only in size. Specs from Hostinger's VPS page as of October 28, 2026.
postParagraphs: Use the table to compare CPU, RAM and storage with your application's requirements. KVM 1 is the smallest listed plan, and your site's load decides whether it is enough. KVM 4 and 8 are for a larger system, a big database or several applications.

contentSections.heading: Maintenance: what is left to you
paragraphs: This is the part the price does not show. On shared hosting, Hostinger maintains the server and the panel; you look after your site (theme, plugins, content). The Premium plan lists weekly backups, and Unlimited includes priority support.

On a VPS, Hostinger says on its own page that, with root access, the server's configuration, updates and security are up to whoever signed up. Hostinger offers templates with the system already installed, such as WordPress, and an automatic weekly backup by default, but maintenance stays with you. In practice, it becomes a list of yours:
bullets: **Configure the environment**: check what the template installs, then adjust the web server, database and certificate for the application.
**Update** the operating system and the programs, from time to time.
**Secure it**: firewall, open ports, passwords and access keys.
**Check backups and know how to restore**: the automatic weekly backup is on by default, but verifying the copy and restoring it stay your job.
**Fix it** when the site goes down outside business hours.
postParagraphs: If you have never opened a terminal, this has a cost: either learning time or someone to do it for you. For an ordinary site, that cost is usually bigger than the price difference between the plans.

contentSections.heading: When a VPS makes sense for an AI agent
paragraphs: One case where a VPS often comes in is not a website: it is an AI assistant running all day, like OpenClaw. Then the question changes, because Hostinger also sells a managed plan for these assistants. If that is your case, the comparison is in [OpenClaw at Hostinger: managed or VPS](/en/reviews/openclaw-hostinger-managed-or-vps) and, to pick the size, in [which KVM for OpenClaw](/en/reviews/best-vps-for-openclaw). This article stays on the website server.

contentSections.heading: Verdict: VPS or shared hosting
contentSections.emphasis: If it were for an ordinary site, I would take Premium, because it costs less and Hostinger looks after the server.
paragraphs: **Shared hosting** for a blog, portfolio, company site or small shop. Server maintenance is Hostinger's job. Among the plans, Premium is the starting point; for a Node.js site or if the site grows, Unlimited or Cloud Startup, before you think of a VPS. Node.js alone does not require a VPS.
**VPS** is worth comparing when you need the control and configuration described in the scenario table. Choose the KVM plan by application requirements and count the administration work in the cost.
**When in doubt, shared hosting.** If the need for a VPS shows up later, it means a new contract, with setup and a site transfer.

contentSections.heading: Frequently asked questions
bullets: Is a VPS faster than shared hosting? Not necessarily. Reserved resources and root access change how you control the environment, but they do not by themselves predict how quickly your site responds. Compare the application's requirements and the plan limits.

Can I start on shared hosting and move to a VPS later? Yes, if the application supports the new environment. It is a new contract, with server setup and a site transfer; shared hosting cannot be converted into a VPS from inside the panel.

Do I need to know Linux to have a VPS? Yes, the basics of the terminal: installing programs, updating the system and reading a log. On shared hosting, everything goes through the panel and no terminal is required.

Can a VPS run WordPress? Yes, including with a pre-installed template. You remain responsible for configuring and maintaining the environment, and capacity depends on the application. On shared hosting, WordPress comes ready in the panel and Hostinger looks after the server.

Does SONAR20 work for people who are already Hostinger customers? Yes, on a new purchase: if you already have an account and buy a new plan or product, you also get the 20%. The renewal of a plan you already have is charged at the list price, with no discount.
